note:
wagmi takes 1.4.3. One release is crossed, 1.4.2 to 1.4.3, and nothing is
skipped, so no skipped release carries a landing section anybody has to read.

The releases: class fix, disruption quiet. No core floor moves. Codex stays at
0.147.0 and Claude stays at 2.1.227, the same values 1.4.2 declared.

The box, measured on wagmi-claw at 20:32Z before this note was written:
claw-members holds two people, jeremiah and abigail. Each has the persistent
core installed, reading 2.1.252 and 2.1.227, and each has codex at 0.147.0. No
member reads as below a floor, so this claw's own classifier will not defer the
release to the quiet window.

An apply now restarts a running wake unit whose program changed. Before this,
the update replaced the program and left the process running the bytes it
started with, so a wake-rail fix reached the machine and did not reach the
member until somebody restarted the unit or the box was rebooted. Both members'
units are running here, both started by hand at 18:45:35 after the 1.4.2 ride,
so this apply prints one restart line per account. Each line names the rail
digest it was running and the one it moved onto. A restart costs at most one
poll interval of delivery: the rail reads the bus cursor rather than a queue, so
the next pass sees the same unread mail.

From this release the wake rail reads the settings file a claw-admin edits. The
file is /etc/commonclaw/bus-nudge.conf, which is where every run has written it,
and the program had been looking at another path. Every key in that file goes
into service on this apply, ENABLED among them. A claw-admin who had set
ENABLED to no will find the rail stopping at this apply, correctly, and until
now nothing has said so. The five keys on this box hold the shipped defaults, so
nothing here changes behaviour today.

Both members read the claude adapter as ready, measured as each member rather
than over the admin door: jeremiah on 10 session sockets under
/run/user/1000/cc-socks, abigail on 10 under /run/user/1001/cc-socks. Neither
account runs a tmux server. A tmux server left running weeks ago would count as
a session and take delivery, which the wake-rail document this release ships now
says on the box.
